root_cause.text: The `ext4_mb_scan_groups` function failed to validate that the starting block group index (`ac->ac_g_ex.fe_group`) was within the valid range of `ngroups`, allowing out-of-bounds indices to initiate the allocation search loop.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (start >= ngroups) start = 0;` in `ext4_mb_scan_groups`, correcting the CVE description's concern that "If ac->ac_g_ex.fe_group is >= ngroups... the very first iteration will call ext4_mb_scan_group() with this unsupported group".

Looking at the ext4_mb_scan_groups function (lines 1096-1179), I can see: 1) ngroups is calculated correctly (line 1105-1108), 2) start is set directly from ac->ac_g_ex.fe_group without any bounds validation (line 1110: 'start = ac->ac_g_ex.fe_group'), 3) This unvalidated start value is then passed to ext4_mb_scan_groups_linear() (line 1113) and other scan functions without checking if start < ngroups. In contrast, the old ext4_mb_find_good_group_xarray function had 'if (WARN_ON_ONCE(start >= end))' validation (line 890), but this validation was not carried over to the new ext4_mb_scan_groups function. The missing bounds check allows out-of-bounds indices to initiate the allocation search loop, confirming the bug is present and unfixed.
